questions.stem: In Data Splitting for data science, into which two subsets does Approach 1 divide a dataset?
options: Training and Validating
Validating and Testing
Training and Testing
Historical and Current
Structured and Unstructured
questions.explanation: Approach 1, widely used by data modellers and data scientists, splits the dataset into a Training subset and a Testing subset.

questions.stem: Which three subsets are used in Approach 2 of Data Splitting for data science?
options: Training, Validating and Testing
Raw, Cleansed and Published
Training, Testing and Production
Sampling, Modelling and Reporting
Silver, Gold and Premium
questions.explanation: Approach 2 adds a Validation stage, so the dataset is divided into Training, Validating and Testing subsets.

questions.stem: In the bank example used to explain Data Splitting, what is the model's aim for the 100,000 customers?
options: To detect fraudulent transactions
To predict which customers will close their accounts
To calculate interest on each account
To tag each customer as Silver, Gold or Premium based on credit history, buying behaviour and transaction values
To merge duplicate customer records
questions.explanation: The example model tags each of the 100,000 bank customers into one of three categories, Silver, Gold or Premium, using their credit history, buying behaviour and transaction values.

questions.stem: In Approach 1 of Data Splitting, how is the model's output judged?
options: By how quickly it runs on the training subset
By the accuracy of its results on the second (Testing) subset
By the number of customers in the dataset
By whether it terminates after a finite number of steps
By the opinion of the business sponsor
questions.explanation: After training on the first subset, the model is run on the second subset to test it, and its output is judged by the accuracy of results on that subset.

questions.stem: When is the three-subset approach to Data Splitting most widely used?
options: When the dataset is very small
When the data is unstructured
When the model is only for internal reporting
When there is no time to test
When it is of utmost importance that the model's output accuracy is at the highest possible value
questions.explanation: Approach 2 is used where output accuracy must be as high as possible; with the extra Validation stage, expected accuracy is mostly at its best.

questions.stem: Where does the Validation stage sit in the three-subset approach to Data Splitting?
options: After Training and before Testing on the third subset
Before Training begins
After Testing has been completed
At the same time as Testing, on the same subset
Only after the model has gone into production
questions.explanation: The model is trained on the first set, its output is evaluated in a Validation stage, and only then is it run on the third set for Testing.

questions.stem: What determines the percentage of data placed in each subset when splitting a dataset for data science?
options: The number of columns in the table
The programming language used
The criticality of the output, such as a marketing model versus a model for cancer patients
A fixed rule of exactly one third per subset
The size of the database server
questions.explanation: The percentages can vary based on the criticality of the output, for example whether the model is for marketing or for cancer patients.

questions.stem: What is the risk of Random Sampling when splitting a dataset?
options: It always requires the latest data
It cannot be used with bank data
It only works within a single country
Valuable data may be unevenly distributed across the subsets
It produces more subsets than required
questions.explanation: Random Sampling divides data randomly, with the risk that valuable data ends up unevenly distributed across the subsets.

questions.stem: A dataset holds customers from ten countries and the data is divided randomly within each country. Which sampling method is this?
options: Random Sampling
Graded Random Sampling
Non-random Sampling
Sequential Sampling
Validation Sampling
questions.explanation: Graded Random Sampling divides data randomly but with parameters, such as splitting randomly within each country, so any uneven distribution is confined to within a country.

questions.stem: Which situation is given as an example of Non-random Sampling when splitting datasets?
options: The subsets must be of equal size
The data comes from ten different countries
The customers are all in one age group
The model must be tested twice
The model requires the latest data
questions.explanation: Non-random Sampling is used where a specific dataset is required, for example when the model needs the latest data.
